intro.h2: You see the real cost of every fixture
paragraphs: Ann Arbor Remodeling is a full-service firm for design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, taking on everything from bathroom renovations to complete home remodels and additions. Every project is designed from scratch, and the team handles the first design concept, permits and construction all the way through final inspection.

Pricing works differently here. Instead of hiding markups in line items, the contract shows what the company pays its trade partners and the direct cost of your finish materials. If a toilet costs them $478, that is the number you see. Owner Justin Kolic wants the company on the same side of the table as its clients.

services.h2: Design-build remodeling in Ann Arbor, from kitchens to additions

items.name: Kitchen remodeling
items.blurb: Custom kitchens planned around how your family cooks, with cabinetry design, material selections and lighting layouts worked out with your designer. The company's directional pricing puts a medium-size kitchen remodel with mid-level finishes at $125k to $175k.

image.alt: Kitchen remodel with navy lower cabinets, white upper cabinets, double stainless wall ovens and white zigzag wall tile

items.name: Bathroom remodeling
items.blurb: Primary suites and hall baths, built by a lead carpenter who stays on your job until it is finished. The newest finished project, the Huron River Primary Suite, pairs a freestanding tub with wood-look tile. Hall bathroom projects are listed at $50k to $55k.

image.alt: Huron River primary suite bathroom with a freestanding tub, wood-look wall tile, black countertop and floating wood vanity

items.name: Basement finishing
items.blurb: Basements fall under the Lead Carpenter System, so the same person is on site each weekday, coordinating trade partners and inspectors. On the company's pricing guide, a 1500-square-foot basement with a bathroom and bar starts at $200k.

image.alt: Finished lower level with white built-in cabinets, open shelving, a wood support post and light wood-look flooring

items.name: Additions, sunrooms and screen porches
items.blurb: Additions begin with a discovery day at your home, opening drywall to confirm conditions so the schedule holds. The team also builds sunrooms and screen porches that connect indoors and out. A 200-square-foot kitchen addition starts at $300k.

image.alt: Sunroom addition with exposed wood beams, two skylights, a ceiling fan and windows on three sides

items.name: Custom woodworking
items.blurb: With its own wood shop and carpenters, the company builds bookcases, fireplace built-ins and mantels, built-in cabinetry and even custom tables, so the storage, shelving and trim in your remodel are made for that exact room.

image.alt: Custom walnut built-in bookcase and cabinet run beside an exposed brick wall

why_choose_us.h2: How Justin's team runs a job

items.title: Transparent contracts
items.text: Your contract lists what the company pays trade partners and the direct cost of your finishes, with no hidden markups tucked into the line items.

items.title: One lead carpenter, one project
items.text: On kitchens, baths and basements, a hands-on lead carpenter manages only your job and is typically on site from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

items.title: Daily logs you can check
items.text: Daily logs, progress photos and change orders post to BuilderTrend, so you know where things stand even if you are across the country.

items.title: Cleaner air while you live there
items.text: Crews set up zip walls and air scrubbers to limit dust and contaminants, which matters when your family stays home during construction.

about.h2: A future teacher who chose the trades
about.text: Justin Kolic decided to become a remodeler in 2003 while studying to be a teacher. He finished an associate degree, took construction management classes at WCC and earned his Michigan Residential Builders license in 2006. He started Ann Arbor Remodeling LLC in 2013. Justin hires for character, following the ideas in The Ideal Team Player, and builds skills on the job. Two of today's team members, a lead carpenter and an estimator, were clients before they joined, and his former WCC instructor now leads pre-construction.

image.alt: Justin Kolic, owner of Ann Arbor Remodeling

process.h2: Four phases from concept to final inspection

steps.title: Conceptual design
steps.text: After the Project Design Agreement, you meet your designer for a detailed measure, then review 2 to 3 concept designs with cost ranges for each.

steps.title: Design development
steps.text: Your designer walks you through cabinetry, materials, plumbing fixtures, lighting and electrical layouts while preparing the final drawing set for permits.

steps.title: Pre-construction
steps.text: You review the contract, plans and final scope, permits are applied for, and you meet the project manager who will run your job.

steps.title: Construction
steps.text: Your project manager shares progress, schedule and changes in Buildertrend and holds milestone meetings, and your designer returns for paint, tile and cabinet install reviews.

service_area.h2: Based on Jackson Plaza in Ann Arbor
service_area.text: The office is at 251 Jackson Plaza E in Ann Arbor, open Monday through Friday from 10 AM to 5 PM. The company has not published a list of the towns it covers, so if you live outside Ann Arbor, call or text (734) 368-1221 and ask whether your project fits. As a small company, it explains that it can't take on every project that comes in, so reach out early.

faq.h2: Questions about pricing, process and the lead carpenter

items.a: The company shares directional prices based on mid-level finishes: a hall bathroom at $50k to $55k, a large primary bathroom at $100k to $160k+, a medium kitchen at $125k to $175k, a 1500-square-foot basement with bath and bar from $200k, and a 200-square-foot kitchen addition from $300k. Your exact cost comes from design and a detailed scope.

items.q: Why do you show your actual costs?
items.a: Ann Arbor Remodeling uses a transparent pricing model. Its construction contracts break out what it pays trade partners and the direct cost of your finish materials, without hidden markups. The company says this puts it on the same side of the table as you and makes talks about scope or material changes more relaxed.

A lead carpenter is a hands-on project manager who runs one project at a time and is on site from start to finish, typically Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. They are your main contact, keep the work area clean, coordinate inspectors and oversee trade partners. Additions and larger projects use a project manager system instead.

items.q: Can we live at home during the remodel?
items.a: Many clients do. The Lead Carpenter System is used for kitchen, bath and basement projects where families stay in the house, and crews set up zip walls and air scrubbers to limit the spread of dust. Daily logs and progress photos in BuilderTrend keep you informed even when you are away.

items.q: How does the design phase work?
items.a: After you sign a Project Design Agreement and pay a deposit, a kickoff meeting introduces your designer and covers a detailed measure. You then see 2 to 3 concept designs with cost ranges, refine one through design development, and receive final drawings for permits before you sign the construction contract.

final_cta.h2: Tell Justin's team what you want to build
final_cta.text: Call or text (734) 368-1221, or email info@annarborremodeling.com, to start the conversation.
